title: PAS-positive foamy macrophages: Whipple disease (chronic bacterial infection)
vignette: A 46-year-old man comes to the office due to abdominal discomfort and diarrhea. The symptoms began 6 months ago, and he has now developed significant weight loss. The patient does not use tobacco or alcohol. Intestinal biopsy is performed, and a periodic acid-Schiff (PAS) stained section of the small-intestinal mucosa shows the lamina propria distended by numerous foamy, PAS-positive (magenta) macrophages containing rod-shaped bacilli. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this patient's symptoms?

clues.note: Chronic diarrhea and abdominal discomfort suggest a small-bowel malabsorption process.
Weight loss over months indicates malabsorption - infected macrophages blocking intestinal lymphatics impair nutrient absorption in Whipple disease.

clues.text: foamy, PAS-positive (magenta) macrophages containing rod-shaped bacilli
clues.note: Lamina propria distended by foamy, PAS-POSITIVE macrophages containing bacilli is the pathognomonic finding of Whipple disease (Tropheryma whipplei), a chronic bacterial infection. PAS stains polysaccharide in the bacterial cell wall a magenta color.

whatMatters: Chronic diarrhea + weight loss (malabsorption) with a small-bowel biopsy showing lamina propria packed with foamy PAS-POSITIVE macrophages containing bacilli = Whipple disease, a CHRONIC BACTERIAL infection by Tropheryma whipplei (a gram-positive actinomycete). Answer A. Treat with prolonged antibiotics (ceftriaxone -> TMP-SMX).
strategy: The PAS-positive foamy macrophages full of rods are the giveaway -> Whipple disease -> chronic bacterial infection (T. whipplei). Match the distractors to their own biopsy pictures: celiac (villous atrophy, intraepithelial lymphocytes), abetalipoproteinemia (clear lipid-laden enterocytes), lactase deficiency (normal histology), viral (self-limited, no PAS+ macrophages).

eliminations.label: Immune-mediated gluten sensitivity - celiac
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: celiac disease, an immune reaction to gluten. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: its biopsy shows villous atrophy, crypt hyperplasia, and intraepithelial lymphocytes - not PAS+ macrophages. ✅ Correct if: malabsorption improving on a gluten-free diet with villous blunting.

eliminations.label: Impaired lipoprotein formation - abetalipoproteinemia
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: an inherited apolipoprotein B defect impairing chylomicron formation. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it presents in infancy with clear lipid-laden enterocytes (and acanthocytes), not PAS+ macrophages in a 46-year-old. ✅ Correct if: infantile fat malabsorption with acanthocytes.

eliminations.label: Lactase deficiency - normal histology
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: brush-border lactase deficiency causing osmotic diarrhea/bloating after dairy. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: histology is NORMAL, and there's no weight loss or foamy macrophages. ✅ Correct if: dairy-triggered symptoms with a normal biopsy.

eliminations.label: Viral infection - acute, self-limited
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: viral gastroenteritis (e.g., norovirus). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it's acute and self-limited (days) in immunocompetent hosts and wouldn't show PAS-positive macrophages. ✅ Correct if: an acute, self-resolving diarrheal illness.

reasoning: Small-bowel biopsy with foamy PAS-positive macrophages containing bacilli in the lamina propria = Whipple disease
Whipple disease is caused by Tropheryma whipplei, a chronic bacterial infection
-> chronic bacterial infection; answer A (treat with prolonged antibiotics)
mechanism: Whipple disease is a rare, systemic, CHRONIC bacterial infection caused by Tropheryma whipplei, a gram-positive actinomycete, most often in middle-aged men. After ingestion, the organism is engulfed by macrophages in the small-intestinal lamina propria but resists killing and replicates within them; accumulation of infected, bacteria-laden macrophages blocks intestinal lymphatics and causes malabsorption with chronic diarrhea, steatorrhea, weight loss, and abdominal pain (with extra-intestinal arthralgia, and cardiac and CNS involvement in later stages). The diagnostic hallmark on small-bowel biopsy is a lamina propria filled with foamy macrophages that are strongly PAS-positive (the periodic acid-Schiff stain highlights polysaccharide in the bacterial cell walls, imparting a magenta color). Treatment is prolonged antibiotics (e.g., ceftriaxone followed by TMP-SMX). The other options are immune (celiac), genetic-metabolic (abetalipoproteinemia), enzymatic (lactase deficiency), or acute viral processes - none produce PAS-positive, bacilli-laden macrophages.

difficulty.label: 📚 Pure knowledge gap
difficulty.message: First Aid GI/Micro > Whipple disease: Tropheryma whipplei, PAS+ foamy macrophages, malabsorption + arthralgia/cardiac/neuro; prolonged antibiotics.

difficulty.label: 🧭 Understanding the question
difficulty.message: PAS-positive macrophages point to a BACTERIAL cause among the malabsorption options.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocabulary
difficulty.message: Unsure on PAS stain, lamina propria, foamy macrophage, actinomycete, or malabsorption? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🧲 Pulled by a distractor
difficulty.message: Celiac (villous atrophy), abetalipoproteinemia (clear enterocytes), lactase deficiency (normal biopsy), and viral (acute) each have a distinct picture - none show PAS+ bacilli-laden macrophages.

difficulty.label: 🖼️ Imaging / diagram
difficulty.message: On the PAS-stained biopsy, the lamina propria is distended by magenta, foamy macrophages stuffed with rods. Anchor: 'PAS-positive foamy macrophages = Whipple (whipplei).'

difficulty.label: ✍️ Something else
difficulty.message: Bank: foamy PAS-positive macrophages with rods = Whipple disease (T. whipplei); chronic bacterial infection; long antibiotic course.
